title: Registration submit contract
description: D18 addendum rule 6 (execution plan §2.6.1; queue items SPEC-REG-NEGOTIATE and SPEC-REG-DECISIONS). A controller submits its controller-owned registration (controller-state-model.schema.json) to the `submit.href` its hub publishes in the capability document (hub-capabilities.schema.json), reads back per element what was accepted, and writes the well-known carrier for anything not accepted. One registration per tenant per identity (`metadata.vendor`, `metadata.product`) is the resource `<submit.href>/<vendor>/<product>`: `PUT` submits or updates it, `GET` reads it with its current element results, `DELETE` retires it. A registration is bound to the credential that created it (its subject, or the shared API_SECRET in single mode); the tenant owner may retire, block, unblock, release, transfer it and free a retired registration's namespaces on the tenant-owner listener, and never edits it. This file defines the request as the conformance fixtures model it, the response, the controller's fallback and its handling of a refused typed write, and the conformance case (specs/sync/conformance/). The prose contract, including the 2026-10-14 decisions, is in the hub-sync design §3.5. Must-ignore applies: no object is closed, and a controller treats an element result, reason code or carrier view it does not know as not accepted.

identity.description: A registration's identity within a tenant: `metadata.vendor` and `metadata.product`. `versionRange` is an attribute of the registration, not part of its identity: a new controller release updates the same registration and keeps older served versions under rule 4.

etag.description: The registration's entity tag: `sha256:` and the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the RFC 8785 canonical JSON of `{"registration": <the registration as submitted>, "state": <state>}` (`registration` is null for a pre-emptive block). It changes whenever the stored registration or its state changes, including a block and an unblock, and never on a no-op. The binding, the credential kind and freed namespaces are not in it, so a release, a transfer or freeing namespaces leaves it unchanged. Sent and compared as an HTTP strong entity tag (quoted on the wire).

otherTerm.description: Rule 3 for a hub-side vocabulary: the shared value `other` with the hub's own term. A reader renders it as "other: <term>"; a controller treats it as a value it does not know.

credentialKind.description: The kind of credential (decision 3). `subject`: a per-tenant subject's token (the device's native credential, D17 row 1). `api-secret`: the deployment's shared API_SECRET, which exists only in single mode (D13). Open vocabulary (rule 3).

binding.description: What a registration is bound to (decision 4): the subject that created it, never its token, so a token rotated on the same subject changes nothing; or the shared secret, which any holder of it presents. A request from any other credential to update or retire the registration is refused 403 `not-registration-owner`. SPEC-REG-INSTANCE binds instances rather than (vendor, product); this shape leaves room for that.

subject.description: The subject's opaque id on the tenant. Required when `kind` is `subject`.

state.description: `active`: typed writes accepted for accepted elements. `retired`: by the controller or the owner; the declaration is kept, frozen, and no typed write is accepted. `blocked`: by the owner (decision 5); the hub refuses the identity on the tenant (403 `blocked-by-owner`), data already stored stays frozen as on retire.

request.description: One request, as the fixtures model it. The controller's `submit` is `PUT <submit.href>/<vendor>/<product>` with the registration as the body and its `retire` is `DELETE` on the same resource, both on the data listener (`ns-api`, or `single`). The owner's actions (`actor: owner`) are on the tenant-owner listener `ns-tenant-admin` (D16), or with API_SECRET on `single`; their paths are proposals: `retire` is `DELETE`, the others `POST <admin registrations path>/<vendor>/<product>/<action>`. Every request carries exactly one precondition: `ifNoneMatch: "*"` to create or to block an identity with nothing stored, `ifMatch: <etag>` otherwise. A request with none is answered 428 (`precondition-required`), so no change is ever blind. `action`, `actor` and `listener` model the method, path and listener of the request, not a vocabulary a controller reads, and are closed.

action.description: `submit` and `retire` by the controller; `retire`, `block`, `unblock`, `release`, `transfer` and `free-namespaces` by the owner (decision 5). The owner never submits.

listener.description: D16. Absent means the data listener. An owner action is authorised on `ns-tenant-admin`, whose listener authenticates the tenant owner (D16; D17 row 2), or on `single` with API_SECRET.

transferTo.description: With `transfer`: the binding the registration takes.

reason.description: Why a registration, an element or a typed write was not accepted, or why a request changed nothing. `code` is an open vocabulary (rule 3): a hub uses `other` with its own `term` for a reason not listed, and a controller treats any reason it does not know as not accepted. `not-registration-owner` (403): the registration is bound to another credential. `blocked-by-owner`: the tenant owner blocked the identity (403 to the controller; 409 to an owner retiring a blocked registration). `not-retired` (409): only a retired registration's namespaces are freed.

term.description: The hub's own term, when `code` is `other`.

path.description: The dotted path in the registration the reason is about, in the form tools/nsschema/sync_model.py `unknown_grammar_fields` uses.

detail.description: Human-readable. A controller must not parse it.

elementResult.description: The result for one element of a stored registration. Elements: `stateSpans/<kind or category>`, `extensions/<namespace>`, `settings.fields/<name>` and `replayInputs/<input>` (the last two for typed fields only). `accepted-with-ignored-members`: accepted, and the listed members of the element are ignored (rule 1). `rejected`: the hub offers no typed API for the element; the controller writes its well-known carrier.

carrierView.description: On an accepted element (decision 7): whether the hub serves older readers a projected, read-only view of its typed records in the carrier's shape. `served`: the controller writes typed only. `not-served`, or absent: typed only, or typed and carrier when the element declares `dualWriteLink`. Open vocabulary (rule 3); a value the controller does not know is not accepted, so the element is written as its carrier. SPEC-REG-INSTANCE specifies the view's mapping.

response.description: The hub's answer to a submit, retire or read. `outcome`: `accepted` (stored; every element accepted, possibly with ignored members), `partial` (stored; at least one element rejected), `rejected` (nothing stored or changed; `reasons` says why), `precondition-failed` (nothing changed; `current` carries the stored etag and state), `not-found` (nothing stored under this identity), `retired` (the registration is retired; stored data is kept), `applied` (an owner action other than retire took effect; `registration` is absent when nothing remains stored). `noop`: the request asked for what was already stored, so nothing changed and the etag is the stored one (a retried create or update succeeds; RFC 9110 §13.1.1 allows a 2xx for If-Match when the requested change has already been applied, and this contract applies the same rule to a create's If-None-Match).

status.description: The HTTP status. 201 created (including a pre-emptive block); 200 updated, retired, read, applied or no-op; 403 the credential may not do this, or the owner blocked the identity; 404 not found; 409 the request conflicts with the registration's state; 412 a precondition failed; 413 too large; 422 rejected for its content; 428 no precondition sent.

registration.description: The stored registration's identity, state and etag after the request, with what it is bound to and the kind of credential that last wrote it (decisions 3 and 4). Absent when nothing is stored.

blockedFrom.description: With state `blocked`: the state the block interrupted, which unblocking restores. Absent for a pre-emptive block, which stores no registration; unblocking that removes it.

boundTo.description: null: released by the owner; the next credential with the permission to update it binds it.

credentialKind.description: The kind of credential that last created or updated the registration; the owner's view shows registrations made with the shared secret (decision 3). Owner actions do not change it.

freedNamespaces.description: Namespaces of this registration the owner freed after it was retired (decision 5). A freed namespace is not held by this registration, so another may claim it.

current.description: With `precondition-failed`: what is stored now, so the controller can read it and resubmit.

reasons.description: Registration-level reasons: why the request was rejected or changed nothing.

ignored.description: Rule 1. Members outside any element that the hub ignores, as dotted paths.

fallbackEntry.description: What the controller writes for one element. `typed`: through the typed API the hub derived. `typed-and-carrier`: an accepted element the hub serves no carrier view of, declaring `dualWriteLink`: written typed and as its carrier, the two linked by the controller's record id (decision 7). `carrier`: the element's well-known carrier (`stateSpans[].wire`, or an extension's `carrier`), as today's documents. `untyped`: a typed setting or replay input is written where it is today and the hub treats it as name-only. `none`: the element has no well-known carrier, so the hub receives nothing for it.

fallback.description: The controller's write plan, one entry per element of its registration, keyed by element id.

blockedFrom.description: With state `blocked`: the state the block interrupted, which unblocking restores. Absent for a pre-emptive block, which stores no registration; unblocking that removes it.

freedNamespaces.description: Namespaces of this registration the owner freed after it was retired (decision 5). A freed namespace is not held by this registration, so another may claim it.

storedRegistration.description: A registration as the hub stores it. `registration` is null only for a pre-emptive block. The binding is in the etag; credential kind, `blockedFrom` and freed namespaces are stored beside the registration, outside it.

conformanceCase.description: One conformance case (specs/sync/conformance/*.yaml): a hub's capability document and stored state, a submitter, a controller's registration and request, and the expected response and controller fallback. All content is synthetic. A hub implementation passes a case when, booted with `capabilities` and `hubState` and sent `request` with `registration` by a credential holding `submitter`, it answers `expected.response` (reason `detail` strings are not compared) and stores `expected.storedAfter` where the case states it. A case with `typedWrite` also states what a controller does when a later typed write is refused (`expected.typedWrite`).

control.description: For a case whose request is rejected, fails a precondition or rejects an element: the id of the passing case that differs from it only in the aspect under test. For a case whose typed write is refused definitely: the case whose typed write is refused for load, differing only in `typedWrite`.

cell.description: The D18 addendum compatibility cell this case exercises.

capabilities.description: The hub's capability document. null: the hub publishes none (an older hub; `/.well-known/nightscout/sync` answers 404).

wellKnownRegistrations.description: The well-known registrations the capability document links to, keyed by `href`.

carrierViews.description: For each element id: what this hub reports as the element's `carrierView` when it accepts it (decision 7). An element not listed has none, which means not served. How a hub decides is SPEC-REG-INSTANCE's.

submitter.description: The credential sending the request: its kind and subject (decisions 3 and 4), its permissions on this tenant (shiro-style, `*` a wildcard part) and, when the hub restricts namespaces, the roots it may claim. No `namespaceRoots`: first to claim (decision 1). A list, even an empty one: the hub restricts the credential to it. `token` labels the token presented; binding ignores it. All values are synthetic.

registration.description: The controller's registration. null: an older controller that has none, or an owner action, which carries no registration (then `expected.fallback` is null and `controllerWouldSubmit` false).

grammarValid.description: Whether `registration` validates against controller-state-model.schema.json. Stated so a case cannot pass by testing an invalid registration where a valid one was meant.

typedWrite.description: A later typed write for one element that the hub refuses (decision 8), after the request's response set the write plan. `status` is the HTTP status of the refusal: 429 or any 5xx is a load refusal, retried with backoff; any other is definite. `retryAfter` the Retry-After seconds, when sent; `reason` the refusal's reason, when given; `deadlinePassed` true when the record's delivery deadline (the controller's) has passed under load refusals, so the record is sent as its carrier and the element stays accepted.

writes.description: For an older controller: documents it writes today, to show which well-known registration describes each.

controllerWouldSubmit.description: Whether a controller following the contract submits at all, given the capability document: it does when the document exists, offers `submit`, and lists its grammar major. A case may still send a request the controller would not, to test the hub.

describedBy.description: For `writes`: the well-known registration (and element, when a kind's wire carrier matches) that describes each write.

storedAfter.description: The stored registration after the request, or null when none is stored.

typedWrite.description: What the controller does about the refused typed write. `retry-backoff`: a load refusal (429 or any 5xx, with or without Retry-After); the record is retried, not written as its carrier and not dropped. `carrier-this-record`: a definite refusal, after which the element is not accepted until the next re-check; or a load refusal past the record's delivery deadline, after which the element stays accepted. `recheck` is always false: a refusal never makes the controller re-read the capability document or its registration. `fallback`: the write plan afterwards.
